notes: P02 task SACMAT-X02_reference_semantics (RQ3): language-independent reference decision oracle for PolicyTrace. evaluation/venue2027/sacmat/reference_semantics.py implements reference_decide(trace, request) -> ReferenceVerdict from first principles — it imports NO candidate policy engine or baseline arm (verified: module imports only stdlib) and may accept PolicyTrace-shaped input (any object/dict exposing .events with kind/principal/tenant/resource/purpose/policy_state/logical_time records) via duck-typed field access without depending on that module. DELEGATE convention: policy_state carries the delegating source, principal is the delegate gaining authority. History is replayed in logical-time order per (tenant, resource, purpose) scope implementing the four mandated semantic axes: (1) grant ordering — authority records carry the logical time they were (re-)established; an access at a decision time before the grant came into force is expiry divergence -> DENY; (2) delegation transitivity — DELEGATE inherits the source's active authority and records edges both forward (BFS cycle detection) and inverted (delegate -> delegators) so multi-hop redelegation chains resolve; a delegation whose source has no active authority at that logical time is UNRESOLVABLE_DELEGATION -> UNKNOWN (never a forced deny); an edge closing a cycle taints every principal on the cycle in scope (delegated consent must be acyclic) -> DENY; (3) revocation dominance — REVOKE removes the actor's authority and is remembered as an epoch; the query principal's authority chain is walked UPSTREAM over the inverted delegation graph so any revoked actor backing inherited authority at or before decision_time denies (revoked-actor transitivity; a downstream redelegation cannot resurrect revoked authority, while a fresh direct GRANT clears the principal's own revocation epoch as a new authority basis); (4) obligation satisfaction — every declared obligation must be strictly satisfied (True), one fault -> DENY. Fail-closed composition: missing/None/non-int logical_time on any event or missing decision_time -> INDETERMINATE MISSING_LOGICAL_TIME (temporal precedence undecidable, never a safe-looking denial); empty/unknown query purpose -> DENY UNKNOWN_PURPOSE; malformed identifiers -> INDETERMINATE MALFORMED_EVENT; empty trace -> DENY EMPTY_TRACE; unsupported event kinds -> UNKNOWN UNSUPPORTED_CONSTRUCT; otherwise ALLOW. Four-valued portable verdict (ALLOW/DENY/INDETERMINATE/UNKNOWN) with stable reason codes, JSON-serializable dataclasses, canonical trace_sha256, no clock/randomness/I/O. test_reference_semantics.py imports only the reference module (independence rule): 8 positive controls (conformant grant->access ALLOW, delegation transitivity ALLOW for two-hop chains, expiry divergence DENY, revocation dominance DENY, re-grant after revocation restores direct authority, satisfied obligations ALLOW, JSON round-trip stability, PolicyTrace-shaped duck-typed input accepted) and 12 adversarial controls (revoke-before-grant DENY, delegation cycle never permits, missing event logical_time -> INDETERMINATE, missing decision_time -> INDETERMINATE, revoked-actor transitive DENY, redelegation chain to revoked root DENY, unknown purpose DENY, purpose mismatch DENY, obligation fault DENY, empty trace DENY, unsupported kind UNKNOWN, unresolvable delegation UNKNOWN) plus malformed-query INDETERMINATE and JSON-serializability checks. 27 passed in 0.25s; uvx ruff@0.7.1 check + format --check clean. source_sha_after records base commit e373f6e4 per sibling convention; the single task commit SHA is created immediately after this report and reported in the handoff.
